static_traits.name: Lin Wei
static_traits.family_status: Parents are from Japan, now living in Toronto, Canada
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues affected by Self-doubt; has a few close friends, but has not yet discussed feelings of insufficiency with them
static_traits.medical_history: Has not experienced similar psychological problems, has not received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic, highly cooperative; negative tone, often using Self-denial and 'should' phrasing, tending to ignore positive information

basic_info.main_problem: Because class exam scores dropped this semester, I feel I am a terrible teacher; this insufficiency emerged at the start of the school year and keeps affecting me.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this incompetence is affecting my mental health and teaching performance.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough/not competent enough

special_situations.event: The class's overall exam scores declined this semester
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If student scores drop, it means my teaching has failed, I am a terrible teacher
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Actively seeks feedback from colleagues and implements new teaching strategies, trying to raise scores quickly
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I let students down, I am a terrible teacher

special_situations.event: Discovering scores below anticipation after each quiz or assignment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One poor quiz score represents overall teaching failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constant self-criticism and overtime lesson prep, while distancing from colleagues to avoid exposing insufficiency
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed,I am not competent enough

special_situations.event: Receiving positive student feedback while seeing low scores
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Without high scores, any positive feedback does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on negative data, ignores positive information
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Scores are the truth; everything else is comforting talk

special_situations.event: At the start of the school year, teaching shifted online and teaching methods changed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must adapt to online teaching immediately and improve all students' grades, otherwise I am unqualified
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to fix all problems at once, working overtime preparing lessons in pursuit of overall improvement
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should do better, must make all students learn

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a competent teacher, helping students achieve good grades
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated as unqualified, worrying about harming students and being blamed for it
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control through self-reproach and urges improvement
Keeps distance from colleagues to avoid being judged
Personalizing student grades entirely to reinforce responsibility

object_relations.object_representation: Others (colleagues, students, managers) experienced as harsh judges

object_relations.self_representation: A caregiver bearing full responsibility for students
object_relations.object_representation: The student group I am responsible for

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor guides reality testing and points out students' positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client views positive feedback as 'not counting', worrying that acknowledging it would seem like evading problems
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing scores as the only standard, negating positive evidence with affirmative sentences, firm but restrained tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether one seeks support from friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client equates sharing troubles with exposing incompetence, worrying about being judged and embarrassed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding with brief negation, avoiding details, reducing emotional vocabulary, cautious tone.

manifestations: Growing distant from colleagues, less interaction
Not yet discussing feelings of insufficiency with close friends
Avoiding help-seeking out of shame and embarrassment

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should / must' to demand of oneself
Uses scores as the absolute standard to evaluate teaching, ignoring positive feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism, fully personalizing student grades
Hesitates to seek help from friends; worries about being judged

positive_force: Actively seeks colleague feedback and implements new teaching strategies
Willing to set specific and feasible improvement goals (focusing on weak subjects)
Students gave positive feedback (finding classes rewarding, enjoying lessons)
Has some social support (several close friends)
negative_force: Fully personalizing student grades, over-attributing to oneself
Tends to label himself a 'terrible teacher'
Negating positive information, focusing only on negative data
Distancing from colleagues out of shame and Self-doubt, avoiding seeking help

target_behavior.behavior: Personalized self-blame and self-labeling when academic evaluation results are unsatisfactory
antecedent: Seeing quiz or exam scores drop
Stress of adapting to online teaching
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating student grades with self-worth, relying on external validation with catastrophic interpretation (low scores mean failure and incompetence)
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a sense of control through self-blame and spurring oneself to double their efforts, escaping facing the more complex influencing factors
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety and Self-doubt worsens, decline in work performance, disturbed sleep and daily life, distancing from colleagues

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding social support and peer interaction
antecedent: Thinks of the embarrassment and shame of talking to friends or colleagues about the trouble
Worrying about being judged as incompetent
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing exposing insufficiency, fearing negative evaluation, equating seeking help with failure
target_behavior.function: Escaping the risk of shame and being evaluated, keeping self-protective boundaries
target_behavior.consequence: Increased sense of isolation, negative emotions maintained, insufficient resource use prolonging the problem
